title: Independent Living Residency Agreement — The Fee Recorded When an Annual Increase Takes Effect
content:
**Clause.** Under the Independent Living Residency Agreement, the fee recorded when an annual increase takes effect is the fee stated in the written notice of that increase mailed to the resident. The fee is recorded in US dollars, to the cent, rounded half up.

## Where the figure comes from

The written notice of an annual increase is recorded on the residency with its mailing date and the proposed fee. The proposed fee on that notice is the noticed fee, and the noticed fee is the figure the clause records.

| Input | Record it is read from |
|---|---|
| Noticed fee | The proposed monthly service fee recorded on the residency with the written notice of the increase |
| Recorded fee | The noticed fee, in dollars and cents |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

A resident's written notice states a proposed monthly service fee of 4,265.40. The fee recorded when the increase takes effect is 4,265.40.

A notice stating a proposed fee of 5,512.875 (a figure carried to a fraction of a cent) is recorded at 5,512.88, the cent being rounded half up.

## Points of judgement

**Which notice counts?** The written notice of that increase mailed to the resident, as recorded on the residency.

**Is the recorded fee a fee per calendar month?** Yes. It is the contracted monthly service fee of the residency.
